 Judgment

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 29.07.2024.
2.

The Brief facts of the case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 29.07.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HG-2339 proceeding near Bhattaramarenahalli Bus stand, Devanahalli-Budigere SH-104, Channarayapatna Hobli, Bangalore Rural District, petitioner was riding slowly carefully, cautiously,
observing the traffic rules, at that time a Car bearing Reg. No. TN-14-E-0724 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came at a high speed and dashed against to the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Akash Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Sathya Sai Hospital, wherein he was treated as inpatient and spent more than Rs.5,00,000/-
towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges.

The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 35 years, the petitioner was working as employee at Alpha Design Technologies Pvt. Ltd., and earning Rs.35,000/- per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest.

sentences.text: After service of notice, respondent No.2 remained absent.
Hence, placed exparte.
The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition.
Further this respondent admits the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further this respondent submitted that, there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. TN-14-E-0724 at the material time and that the unfortunate accident was solely attributable to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself, who was riding motorcycle without helmet and DL at a high speed, unmindful of the movements of other motor vehicles and negligent all the traffic rules and regulations.
It is further submitted that, the accident in question took place solely due to the carelessness and negligent of the petitioner.
Further this respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, framed the following issues are as under:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he is the victim of the motor vehicle accident caused by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. TN-14-E-0724 on 29.07.2024 at about 06.00 p.m., near Bhattaramarenahalli Bus stand, Devanahalli-Budigere SH-104, Channarayapattana Hobli, Bangalore Rural District and sustained injuries as pleaded in the petition?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What order or Award?
5.
In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.12 and closed his side.
On the other hand, no evidence is lead on behalf of the respondents.

6. Heard the arguments and perused the materials placed on record.
7.
My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:

:REASONS:
8.
ISSUE No.1:

The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.

sentences.text: The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 12.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P.2 is the Complaint, Ex.P.3 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.5 is the Wound certificate, Ex.P.6 is the Charge-sheet, Ex.P.7 is the Notice U/s 133 of M. V. Act, Ex.P.8 is the Reply Notice, Ex.P.9 is the Discharge Summary, Ex.P.10 is the Medical Bills, Ex
.P.11 and 12 are the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card and Driving License.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 29.07.2024 at about 06.00 p.m.,
petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HG-2339 proceeding near Bhattaramarenahalli Bus stand, Devanahalli- Budigere SH-104, Channarayapatna Hobli, Bangalore Rural District, petitioner was riding slowly carefully, cautiously, observing the traffic rules, at that time a Car bearing Reg. No. TN-14-E-0724 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner, came at a high speed and dashed against to the petitioner motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner fell down and sustained several grievous injuries on vital parts of the body.

Immediately, he was shifted to Akash Hospital, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Sathya Sai Hospital,
wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Chennarayapatana Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.95/2024.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
11.
The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Chennarayapatana Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P.2.

On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No.
95/2024.
The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P.1 along with complaint.
12. Ex.P.1 to 8 are the only documents, which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving by the driver of offending vehicle.

The Ex.P.3 (spot panchanama), clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information, held investigation and filed the Ex.P.6, Charge-Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle U/s. 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
The Ex.
P.4 i.e.
, certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

13. It must be noted that, in the cross- examination of PW.1, it is suggested by the learned counsel for respondent No.1 that, petitioner himself hit the offending vehicle, but witness denied the said suggestion.
No matter whether PW.1 admits the said suggestion or not, but in my opinion, the said suggestion is sufficient to conclude that, respondent No.1 has admitted the accident.

In other words,
it is well settled that, suggestion is the reflection of the case of the opponent.

Therefore, in my view,
by posing a suggestion to the effect that, the accident had occurred because of the negligence of the rider of motorcycle and the respondent No.1 has admitted that, the accident in question had happened.

sentences.text: The next question would be, on whose fault accident has occurred.

This question arises because at para No.3 of the written statement filed by respondent No.1, in which the respondent No.1 has raised the specific defence that, the accident had happened due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
Thus, the question would be whether this say of the respondent No.1 can be accepted or not.

It is true that, in the cross-examination of petitioner/PW.1, learned counsel for respondent No.1 has posed question to the PW.1 that, accident is happened due to the negligence of petitioner himself,
but PW.1 had denied the said suggestion.
However, it is important to note that, the second respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Further, the second respondent has not adduced any evidence before the Court.
Besides, the respondents have neither adduced any evidence not produced any documents before this Court.

Thus, these facts, make it clear that, except allegations,
the respondent No.1 has not made any efforts to show that, accident had happened because of the fault of the rider of motorcycle.
15. As stated above, respondents have not produced any evidence before this court to show that, the accident is not caused due to the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thus, the above discussion makes it clear that, except barred allegations, the respondent No.1 has not made any efforts to show that, the accident had happened because of the fault of the petitioner.
It is well settled that, in Motor vehicle accident compensation cases, the strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view of this Court receives support from the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in (2009)
13 SCC 530 between Bimla Devi and others Vs. HRTC.

entities.text: Bimla Devi and others Vs. HRTC
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, I opine that, these facts are sufficient to conclude that, the accident had happened because of the rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. TN-14-E-0724.
16.
The next question would be, whether the petitioner sustained injuries in the accident or not.
It must be noted that, the Ex.P.5 i.e., Wound Certificate shows that, the petitioner was admitted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic and Multi-Speciality Hospital on 29.07.2024.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopaedic and Multi-Speciality Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further, Wound Certificate shows that, the injury sustained by the petitioner is grievous in nature.
Further, in the said Wound Certificate it is mentioned that, petitioner admitted to the hospital with alleged history of RTA.
These facts are not denied by the respondent No.1.
Hence, these facts are sufficient to conclude that,
petitioner
has sustained injuries in the accident
. Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:

The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic & Multi- Speciality Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.

entities.text: Sathya Sai Orthopaedic & Multi- Speciality Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

18. In the petition as well as in his evidence PW.1 deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to Sathya Sai Orthopaedic & Multi-Speciality Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P.9.
Further the petitioner has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.5, wherein the doctor has opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.
19. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 20 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.10 to the tune of Rs.97,425/-.

sentences.text: Further the petitioner contended that, prior to the accident he was an employee at Alpha Design Technologies Pvt. Ltd., and was drawing salary of Rs.35,000/- per month, but in order to prove the said fact petitioner has not produced any relevant evidences.

During the course of cross- examination PW.1 admits that, he re-joined the company after 45 days from the date of accident and his Company paid salary during the said period by converting EL.
21.
In this case the petitioner has neither adduced the evidence of doctor nor produced any disability certificate to show that he has become permanently disabled.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income or under any other heads.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- including the medical expenses.
22. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. TN-14- E-0724 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle punishable U/s 281 and 125(a) of BNS.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1 for the period from 15.06.2024 to 14.06.2025.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 29.07.2024.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.2 owner.
23. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
24. ISSUE No.3:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I. M. V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
